findings.title: Backup-code login can bypass password check
findings.body: authorize() skips password verification when credentials.totpCode is truthy, but takes the backup-code branch whenever credentials.backupCode is truthy. An attacker who knows a victim's email and one valid backup code can send password=wrong, totpCode=anything, backupCode=valid. The password check is skipped because totpCode is present, the backup-code check succeeds, and login returns success. This reduces 2FA to single-factor (backup code only) and allows account takeover without the password. Password must be verified for CAL users regardless of second-factor fields.

findings.title: OAuth/SAML users blocked from using backup codes
findings.body: The early guards throw ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled and IncorrectEmailPassword when credentials.totpCode is missing, without considering credentials.backupCode. A Google/SAML user with 2FA who loses their authenticator and submits only email+backupCode via the lost-access UI will always hit the third-party error and can never use a backup code. The checks must also accept backupCode as satisfying the second-factor presence.

findings.title: Backup-code match is case-sensitive and whitespace-sensitive
findings.body: Generated codes are lowercase hex but displayed with placeholder XXXXX-XXXXX and formatted with a dash, so users will naturally type uppercase or paste with spaces/newlines. The code only does replaceAll("-","") and indexOf, with no toLowerCase() or trim(). A correct code typed in uppercase or with surrounding whitespace fails with IncorrectBackupCode, causing false lockout. Same pattern exists in the disable endpoint. Normalize case and whitespace before comparison.

findings.title: Non-string backupCode crashes disable endpoint
findings.body: The handler guards only truthiness of req.body.backupCode then unconditionally calls req.body.backupCode.replaceAll. If a client sends a truthy non-string JSON value such as a number, array, or object, replaceAll throws TypeError, producing an unhandled 500 instead of a 400 IncorrectBackupCode. Validate typeof backupCode === 'string' before string operations.

findings.title: Backup-code single-use check has TOCTOU race
findings.body: Login does read-decrypt-indexOf-encrypt-write as separate steps: it reads backupCodes, finds the index, sets that slot to null, and writes back. Two concurrent logins with the same backup code can both read the same array before either writes, both find the code, and both succeed. This allows replay of a supposedly single-use backup code. The consume must be atomic via transaction, row lock, or optimistic concurrency.

findings.title: No test for backup-code login or disable
findings.body: The PR adds backup-code generation, login via credentials provider, and disable via backup code, including single-use invalidation and new error codes. The e2e file explicitly leaves TODO for login + disabling with backup and only asserts download filename and copy toast. There is no automated proof that a valid backup code logs in, that reuse fails, or that disable with backup works, leaving the critical auth paths uncovered.
